analyses.what_happens: How to read the trace: the i_clk_wr and i_clk_rd columns are constant, but the state changes at every step. So, as in SymbiYosys with one global clock, both domains step at every column (equal, coincident clocks). Sequence: col1 i_rst_n_wr=1, i_rst_n_sw=0, so the write FSM goes RUN->REQ and busy=1 from col2. col2 i_rst_n_rd=1, so the read FSM sees the request (RST at col3, ACK and ack=1 at col4). col4 the write FSM sees ack and goes to PTR (col5). col5 i_rst_n_sw=0 again, a new low pulse while the FSM is in PTR. In PTR, w_sw_rst_fall = ~i_rst_n_sw & ~reg_sw_rst_req_d = 1, so reg_sw_rst_pend=1 from col6. col6 i_rst_n_sw=1 in HOLD, so REL at col7. col7 the read side releases (ack=0 at col8). col8 REL exits to RUN, so busy=0 at col9. col9 the FSM is in RUN with reg_sw_rst_pend=1, so it goes to REQ and busy=1 at col10. At col9 the checker samples busy=0 and i_rst_n_sw=1 and expects busy=0 at col10, but col10 has busy=1 (nnc_fv_s_CHK_008=1 at col10). Inputs are legal: hardware resets follow ENV-01..04, and nothing forbids a second i_rst_n_sw pulse during a sequence.
analyses.spec_says: spec/SyncFIFO_Design_Specification.md:156 REQ-SRST-008: "A request that arrives while a sequence is running (a low pulse in REL, or a second pulse) shall be served as a new sequence when the write FSM is back in RUN." (rules.json SF-3-47/SF-3-48). :565 "A new low level during REL is served after the write FSM is back in RUN" (SF-10.7-10). :154 REQ-SRST-006: busy "shall be 1 from the cycle after the write FSM takes the request until the cycle in which the write FSM is back in RUN" (SF-3-44). :734 SVA-010: "o_sw_rst_busy is 1 exactly while the write FSM is not in RUN (one cycle behind the state)". :560 "The write FSM leaves RUN, o_sw_rst_busy rises in the next cycle". CHK-008 lists SF-3-33, SF-3-44, SF-6.2-02, SF-10.1-02, SF-10.7-02 and SF-15.3-14, but not SF-3-47 or SF-10.7-10. So a second pulse is legal, and the spec requires it to start a new sequence after RUN is reached.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_sfifo_wr.sv:234 w_sw_rst_fall = ~i_rst_n_sw & ~reg_sw_rst_req_d. :242-243 in REQ and PTR, pend |= fall. :248-249 in REL, pend |= ~i_rst_n_sw. :202 in RUN, `if (!i_rst_n_sw || reg_sw_rst_pend)` goes to REQ. :269 reg_sw_rst_busy <= (next state != RUN). So busy is 0 for exactly the one RUN cycle (col9) and then rises again with i_rst_n_sw=1. This matches REQ-SRST-008 and SVA-010 (busy one cycle behind the FSM state).
analyses.checker_does: verif/sva/nnc_chk_srst.sv:34: `(o_sw_rst_busy == 1'b0) |=> (o_sw_rst_busy == !$past(i_rst_n_sw))`. Part (b) requires busy to stay 0 whenever busy=0 and i_rst_n_sw=1 are sampled. It has no state for a request taken during the previous sequence, so it forbids the new sequence that REQ-SRST-008 requires.

candidates.evidence_for: The DUT does what REQ-SRST-008 (spec:156) and SF-10.7-10 (spec:565) require: the second pulse at col5 is remembered (wr.sv:243) and served from RUN (wr.sv:202). Busy falls for the RUN cycle and rises again, which is SVA-010 (spec:734) and REQ-SRST-006 (spec:154). The assertion (chk_srst.sv:34) has no pending-request term, and its rule list leaves out SF-3-47 and SF-10.7-10. Contract CHK-024 avoids this case in simulation ("Pulses that start and end before o_sw_rst_busy falls are not driven"), which is why simulation never hit it.
candidates.evidence_against: CHK-008 behavior (b) is written without exception in contract.json, and CHK-024(b) also says busy=0 and i_rst_n_sw=1 normally keep it idle. The writer of the contract may have expected a pending request to keep busy high with no 0 cycle.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec does not say whether a served pending request gives a one-cycle busy=0 gap (FSM back in RUN) or a continuous busy=1. It also does not say whether that RUN cycle counts as 'ready for writes' (SF-10.7-07, spec:565). The RTL chose the gap.
candidates.evidence_against: The words of REQ-SRST-006, REQ-SRST-008 and SVA-010 together fix the gap: the FSM is back in RUN for one cycle and busy follows the state one cycle late. So the busy waveform itself is defined.

candidates.evidence_for: The failure needs an i_rst_n_sw low pulse during a running sequence, and contract CHK-024 does not drive such pulses.
candidates.evidence_against: No spec rule forbids this. REQ-SRST-008 (spec:156) makes it a supported case. An assumption that forbids it would hide REQ-SRST-008 behavior, and the spec does not support it.

candidates.evidence_for: None for the busy waveform. The RTL busy timing matches spec:154, :156 and :734.
candidates.evidence_against: The RTL implements REQ-SRST-008 as written.

analyses.options: B (most likely): extend nnc_chk_srst.sv with a pending-request model built from the ports, as the spec describes. Set pend_m at an i_clk_wr edge where o_sw_rst_busy=1, i_rst_n_sw=0 and the i_rst_n_sw sampled at the previous edge was 1 (a new low during the sequence). Clear pend_m at the edge where busy=0 is sampled. Then (b) becomes `busy==0 && i_rst_n_sw && !pend_m |=> busy==0`, and add `busy==0 && pend_m |=> busy==1` so that REQ-SRST-008 is also checked. Add SF-3-47 and SF-10.7-10 to CHK-008. This makes the check stricter, not weaker. C (if the designer wants busy to stay 1 across back-to-back sequences): amend REQ-SRST-006/008 and SVA-010, change wr.sv:269 so busy stays 1 when a pending request is served, and keep the checker with the same pending model.

analyses.what_happens: Both domains step at every column (constant clock columns, one global clock). col1 i_rst_n_wr=1, i_rst_n_rd=0, i_rst_n_sw=0, so REQ and busy=1 from col2. i_full_thr changes 8->5 at col2, while i_rst_n_rd was 0 at col1, which ENV-04 allows. i_rst_n_sw stays 0 for col1-col5: REQ (col2-4), ack at col4, PTR at col5, HOLD at col6. col6 i_rst_n_sw=1, so REL at col7. The read side leaves ACK at col8. col8 i_rst_n_sw=0 (a low in REL), so reg_sw_rst_pend=1 (wr.sv:249), and in the same edge REL->RUN, so busy=0 at col9. col9: i_rst_n_sw=1, busy=0, i_rst_n_rd=1, so the antecedent is true. The checker model has occ_q=0 (block_w was 1 at col8), so it expects o_full=0, but the DUT drives o_full=1. The o_full_thr part holds: expected (0>=5)=0, DUT (i_full_thr==0)=0. The read at col3 and the write at col5 were blocked and do not matter. The FIFO is empty.
analyses.spec_says: spec:527 (10.6, write domain): "block | o_sw_rst_busy flop OR i_rst_n_sw = 0". spec:534 "o_full | block OR full flop". spec:535 "o_full_thr | if block: (i_full_thr equals 0), otherwise the full-threshold flop" (SF-10.6-03). spec:565 "The FIFO is ready for writes when o_sw_rst_busy is 0 and i_rst_n_sw is 1" (SF-10.7-07, also in REQ-SRST-006 spec:154, SF-3-45). spec:243 o_sw_rst_busy: "writes are possible again when it is 0". spec:142 REQ-IF-002: o_full is a flop "combined with the software reset block term by one gate". spec:134 REQ-FUNC-004 allows o_full=1 while a place is free only "because the freed place is not yet visible in the write domain". On the other side, spec:156 REQ-SRST-008 requires the pending request to be served from RUN, but it does not add it to the block term.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_sfifo_wr.sv:135 `assign w_block = reg_sw_rst_busy | ~i_rst_n_sw | reg_sw_rst_pend;`, with the comment at :134 "A pending new request (REQ-SRST-008) also blocks in its RUN cycle". :285 `o_full = w_block | reg_full`. So at col9, with busy=0, i_rst_n_sw=1 and an empty FIFO (reg_full=0), o_full=1 only because reg_sw_rst_pend=1. That is a third block term that the spec does not define. :139 also rejects any write in that cycle.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_wr.sv:38 block_w = !i_rst_n_sw || o_sw_rst_busy, which is the spec:527 definition. :54-70 occ_q is cleared while blocked and counts accepted writes and reads afterwards. :79-82 checks, when i_rst_n_sw && !o_sw_rst_busy && i_rst_n_rd, that o_full == (occ_q == DEPTH) and (after r1) o_full_thr == (occ_q >= i_full_thr). At col9 occ_q=0, so it expects o_full=0.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec defines the write block term with exactly two inputs, busy flop OR i_rst_n_sw=0 (spec:527), and o_full = block OR full flop (spec:534). It states that writes are ready when busy=0 and i_rst_n_sw=1 (spec:565, :154, :243). The RTL adds reg_sw_rst_pend to the block (wr.sv:135), so o_full=1 on an empty FIFO with busy=0 and i_rst_n_sw=1. This is not the conservative case that REQ-FUNC-004 (spec:134) allows. The checker follows spec:527/534 exactly.
candidates.evidence_against: The RTL comment (wr.sv:134) shows the choice was deliberate for REQ-SRST-008. A write accepted in that single RUN cycle is flushed by the new sequence that starts next, so blocking it is harmless for data and arguably cleaner. The spec does not say that writes must be accepted in that cycle.

candidates.evidence_for: REQ-SRST-008 (spec:156) makes the FSM pass through RUN with a request already pending, but the spec does not say whether that RUN cycle is blocked. The block definition (spec:527) and 'ready when busy=0 and i_rst_n_sw=1' (spec:565) say it is not blocked. A word written there is discarded at once by REQ-SRST-005, which suggests a designer might want it blocked. The spec does not decide between these.
candidates.evidence_against: The normative text that exists (spec:527, :534, :565, :243) is explicit and contradicts the RTL. Only intent is in doubt, not the wording.

candidates.evidence_for: The checker has no model of the pending request, so it cannot express the RTL's extra block cycle.
candidates.evidence_against: The checker's block_w and o_full model are the spec definitions (spec:527, :534). Adding the pending term to the checker would contradict the spec as written.

candidates.evidence_for: The failure needs an i_rst_n_sw low during REL. The i_full_thr change at col2 happens while i_rst_n_rd=0, and the spec allows it ("not changed while the FIFO is in use").
candidates.evidence_against: REQ-SRST-008 and SF-10.7-10 (spec:156, :565) explicitly make a low level during REL legal. No environment rule is broken. ASM-004 (spec:884) is about writes, not i_rst_n_sw.

analyses.options: A (most likely, per spec:527/534/565): remove reg_sw_rst_pend from w_block in wr.sv:135, so the block term is busy | ~i_rst_n_sw. Keep pend only for the FSM transition (wr.sv:202) so REQ-SRST-008 is still served. o_full and o_full_thr then follow the spec in the RUN cycle. A write accepted there is discarded by the new sequence. CHK-008 must still get the pending model (see the CHK-008 entry). C (if the designer wants that RUN cycle blocked): amend spec 10.6 (block = busy OR i_rst_n_sw=0 OR pending request), REQ-SRST-002/006, SF-10.7-07, the o_sw_rst_busy port meaning (spec:243) and REQ-IF-002. Then change CHK-009/010/011 to use a port-level pending flag (set by a new i_rst_n_sw low sampled while busy=1, cleared when busy=0 is sampled) as part of BLOCK_W. This keeps the checks at full strength.

analyses.what_happens: Both domains step at every column. col1 i_rst_n_sw=0, so REQ and busy=1 from col2. col2-3 i_rst_n_sw=1, the read side goes RST then ACK (ack=1 at col4). col4 i_rst_n_sw=0 again while the FSM is in REQ, a second pulse: w_sw_rst_fall=1, so reg_sw_rst_pend=1 from col5. In the same edge ack is seen, so PTR (col5), HOLD (col6), REL (col7). col8 i_rst_n_sw=0 in REL, the read side is released, so REL->RUN and busy=0 at col9 (pend still 1). col9: i_wr_en=1, i_rst_n_sw=1, busy=0, and o_full=1 (driven only by reg_sw_rst_pend; the FIFO is empty). The checker expects o_overflow=1 at col10 (wr_en & o_full & sw & !busy). The DUT drives reg_overflow = i_wr_en & ~w_block & reg_full = 0, and busy=1 again at col10.
analyses.spec_says: spec:138 REQ-FUNC-008: o_overflow is a one-cycle pulse "in the cycle after a write was requested while o_full was 1 and writes were not blocked by the software reset". spec:536 "o_overflow | flop: i_wr_en AND NOT block AND full flop, one cycle later" (SF-10.6-04). spec:527 block = "o_sw_rst_busy flop OR i_rst_n_sw = 0". spec:534 o_full = block OR full flop. spec:150 REQ-SRST-002 "A blocked write shall not raise o_overflow". spec:565 "The FIFO is ready for writes when o_sw_rst_busy is 0 and i_rst_n_sw is 1". spec:156 REQ-SRST-008, the pending request served from RUN.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_sfifo_wr.sv:135 w_block includes reg_sw_rst_pend. :285 o_full = w_block | reg_full gives 1 at col9 on an empty FIFO. :188 reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & ~w_block & reg_full gives 0, because the write is treated as blocked. The RTL's own rule is consistent (blocked, so no pulse), but its block term has a third input that spec:527 does not have.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_wr.sv:87-88: `1'b1 |=> (o_overflow == ($past(i_wr_en) && $past(o_full) && $past(i_rst_n_sw) && !$past(o_sw_rst_busy)))`. This is spec:536 with the port o_full in place of the full flop, which is the same thing when the spec block term (busy | ~sw) is 0. At col9 the port-visible block is 0 and o_full=1, so it expects a pulse.

candidates.evidence_for: Same root cause as CHK-010. Under the spec definitions (spec:527, :534), with busy=0 and i_rst_n_sw=1 on an empty FIFO, o_full must be 0. The write would then be accepted and no pulse expected, so the checker would pass. The DUT instead shows o_full=1 with no overflow pulse, which looks to the port like a full, unblocked FIFO that drops a write silently. That contradicts REQ-FUNC-008 (spec:138) as seen at the interface, and SF-10.7-07 (spec:565). The extra block term is at wr.sv:135.
candidates.evidence_against: wr.sv:134 shows the RTL designer deliberately blocks the RUN cycle that serves a pending REQ-SRST-008 request. Inside that view the RTL is self-consistent: a blocked write raises no overflow (spec:150).

candidates.evidence_for: The spec does not say whether the single RUN cycle between two software-reset sequences (REQ-SRST-008, spec:156) blocks writes. If it does, the port-level definition of 'blocked' (busy or i_rst_n_sw low) used by REQ-FUNC-008, REQ-SRST-002 and CHK-011 is incomplete.
candidates.evidence_against: spec:527 defines block explicitly, and spec:565 / :243 say writes are possible when busy=0 and i_rst_n_sw=1.

candidates.evidence_for: The checker's notion of 'blocked' uses only the ports and does not include a pending request.
candidates.evidence_against: That is exactly the spec block definition (spec:527). Changing it without a spec change would contradict the spec.

candidates.evidence_for: The failure needs i_rst_n_sw pulses during a running sequence (col4 in REQ, col8 in REL), and contract CHK-024 does not drive these in simulation.
candidates.evidence_against: REQ-SRST-008 / SF-10.7-10 (spec:156, :565) make such pulses legal. No spec rule puts this on the environment. i_wr_en=1 at col9 with busy=0 and i_rst_n_sw=1 does not break ASM-004 (spec:884).

analyses.options: A (most likely): same fix as CHK-010. Remove reg_sw_rst_pend from w_block (wr.sv:135) but keep it in the FSM RUN->REQ condition (wr.sv:202). In the RUN cycle o_full then equals reg_full (0 when empty), the write is accepted and later flushed, and o_overflow follows spec:536. C (if the designer confirms that RUN cycle must be blocked): amend spec 10.6 block, REQ-FUNC-008, REQ-SRST-002/006, SF-10.7-07 and the o_sw_rst_busy port meaning. Then add the same port-level pending flag to BLOCK_W in CHK-009/010/011, so a write rejected in that cycle needs no pulse and o_full=1 is required there. That is a stricter, spec-backed check, not a weaker one. One fix decision covers CHK-010 and CHK-011 together, and the CHK-008 checker update is needed in both options.
